stories.title: Making architecture decisions arguable instead of announced
stories.line: The practice stuck across projects and became the thing new decisions were expected to arrive with.

stories.title: High availability for a bot runtime that insisted on being in memory
stories.line: The platform ran multi-container with state that survived restarts.

stories.title: Wanting to build it in house and buying instead
Taking a component out of the stack instead of adding one
stories.line: The dependency came out, the dual-write and its rollback logic went with it.

stories.title: One model for everyone, or one per customer
stories.line: Written side by side with the concurrency maths attached.

stories.title: A cache that remembered the failures
stories.line: Failed runs stopped poisoning later ones, and a retry became an actual retry.

stories.title: Tables that arrived in the client's document as raw markup
stories.line: The class of defect went away rather than the three instances of it.

stories.title: Credentials in git history, and rotating keys was not enough
stories.line: The repositories moved with the secrets removed from every commit.

stories.title: Holding back an accuracy number that would have looked great
stories.line: The inflated figure never reached a customer-facing claim.

stories.title: A hiring process that does not depend on me being in the room
stories.line: The panel format and independent-feedback rule became how the round was run.

stories.title: A one out of five, written so the candidate could act on it
stories.line: The rejection was reviewable rather than a verdict.

stories.title: Finding out what the cloud bill was actually for
stories.line: Pruning followed the inventory rather than guesswork.

stories.title: Being asked to pull a date forward, and naming the real constraint
stories.line: The conversation moved from when can you have it to which of these are we willing to do.

stories.title: A port that turned out not to be a port
stories.line: Two findings changed the order of work without changing the plan.

stories.title: Asking what onboarding was supposed to produce
stories.line: Onboarding for that module ran against a stated target and a first-production-value date instead of a feeling.

stories.title: Treating a tee-time booking as a reservation system
stories.line: The product launched with a press release and went out to a user base of twenty thousand.

stories.title: Overturning a hiring verdict by doing the review myself
stories.line: The decision changed on the merits and the reviewer could see exactly which observation I accepted and which I did not.

stories.title: Taking services away instead of adding them
stories.line: Fewer moving parts to deploy, fewer cross-service failures to trace.
